- The app redirects / to /login (302)
- Bogus login returns 200 (graceful, re-renders login page — meaning the app processed the POST and rendered a response, not a 500)

Wait, actually the bogus login returned HTTP 200 with the login page title. That could mean it either (a) failed and re-rendered login, or (b) always returns 200. Let me check the login controller logic to understand.

Let me look at the app code to understand the auth flow, and also check whether there's a demo/default credential I can test. Actually, let me check the app's login controller.

Let me also verify the composer/npm install worked by checking that the app can actually boot (which it does — we're getting valid HTML responses). The fact that the login page renders fully with all assets means the PHP app (Smarty templates, config, DB connection for session) is working.

Let me look at how login works to determine if I can do a real authenticated check. Let me check the app structure.

Actually, the strongest evidence I can gather without modifying the install: verify a genuine authenticated session. The installer already did this. But let me try to independently verify by examining whether I can find the password.
